evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/sell/page.tsx:723-746 — the final 'Publish' button's onClick runs `const stepErrors = validateStep(...); setErrors(stepErrors); if (Object.keys(stepErrors).length === 0) setSubmitted(true);` (also at line 730). It NEVER sends the collected listing to any API: `grep -c 'fetch|mutate|axios|useQuery|RealtorApi|await ' sell/page.tsx` returns 0 across the whole 848-line file. The form's initial data and step config are imported from `./_mock` (`INITIAL_FORM_DATA`, `SELL_STEPS`, line 16).

Full dataflow traced: all property fields are held in local `form` state; on Publish, `submitted` flips to true (page.tsx:730) and the component early-returns a success screen (`if (submitted)` at line 151, rendering `t('submittedTitle')`/`t('submittedBody')`). No create-listing mutation, no POST, no reality-api-client hook is invoked anywhere in the file.

Impact: data loss on a public, conversion-critical flow. A seller completes the entire multi-step wizard (address, price, area, rooms, description, contact details, terms acceptance), clicks Publish, and is shown a success confirmation — but nothing is ever persisted or transmitted. Every submission is silently discarded; no listing is created and no lead is captured.

Confidence HIGH (static-only but fully traced): the complete onClick -> setSubmitted -> success-screen path is confirmed by direct read, and the total absence of any network/mutation call is confirmed by `grep -c` returning 0 over the entire file. The `/[locale]/sell` route is public and reachable in production.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): wire the Publish handler to the generated create-listing mutation from @ppt/reality-api-client (make the handler async, await the mutation, set `submitted` only on success, and render a submit-error state on failure — mirroring the already-correct await+try/catch+setSaveError pattern in the sibling edit page account/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx:195-217). Single-package reality-web edit; verifies with typecheck/test + biome.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/report/page.tsx:37-41 — `handleSubmit` is `(e) => { e.preventDefault(); if (!problem || !description.trim() || !gdprAccepted) return; setSubmitted(true); }`. It validates the form and the GDPR checkbox, then flips local `submitted` state and renders a success screen (`if (submitted)` at line 43) WITHOUT ever POSTing the report. No fetch / mutation / reality-api-client call exists in the file; problem options are imported from `./_mock` (`REPORT_PROBLEMS`, line 11).

This is an integration gap, not a backend-not-ready case: reality-server already exposes a report-submission endpoint (see done backlog rows `code-review-reality-server-submit-report-no-rate-limit`, `code-review-reality-server-report-contact-unvalidated`, which review the server-side submit-report handler). The reality-web page simply never calls it.

Impact: trust/safety. A user reporting a problematic listing (fraud, scam, wrong data) fills the form, accepts GDPR, submits, and sees a confirmation — but the report is silently dropped and never reaches moderators. Users believe abuse has been reported when it has not.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the handler body and the absence of any network call are confirmed by direct read; the matching server endpoint's exact contract was inferred from existing backlog rows rather than re-read this run.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): make `handleSubmit` async and call the generated report-submission hook from @ppt/reality-api-client, setting `submitted` only on success and surfacing a submit-error branch on failure. Single-package reality-web edit; verifies with typecheck/test + biome.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:17,65,268,346,384 — the profile route renders entirely from hardcoded fixtures imported from `./_mock`: `const profile = MOCK_PROFILE` (line 65), `MOCK_LISTINGS.map(...)` (268), `MOCK_ACTIVITY.map(...)` (346), `MOCK_REVIEWS.map(...)` (384). There is no `useQuery`/SDK call and no auth-context read to fetch the current user's real profile, listings, activity, or reviews.

The file's own header comment (lines 8-11) acknowledges this is a placeholder: '...instead of seeing the placeholder MOCK_PROFILE ... replace MOCK_* with live data via the SDK.' The route is nonetheless a shipped, user-reachable page.

Impact: completeness / correctness. Every authenticated user who opens their profile sees the same fabricated identity, listing set, activity log, and reviews rather than their own data — misleading and unusable for its stated purpose. On a public portal this also risks displaying fictitious listings/reviews as if real.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the mock-only data sourcing is confirmed by direct read; classified MEDIUM (not HIGH) because the file comment marks it as a known, intentional placeholder pending SDK wiring rather than a regression.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): replace the MOCK_* references with the generated current-user / my-listings / my-reviews hooks from @ppt/reality-api-client, with loading and empty states. If the live endpoints are not all available yet, split into a smaller finding for the covered subset. Single-package reality-web edit; verifies with typecheck/test + biome.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/home/FeaturedListings.tsx:20-22 — handleToggleFavorite calls toggleFavorite.mutate({ listingId, isFavorite }) fire-and-forget with no onError callback, and the component never reads toggleFavorite.isError/.error. The heart control (passed to every ListingCard via onToggleFavorite on the public homepage) therefore has no failure feedback.

Hook contract traced: frontend/packages/api-client... actually frontend/packages/reality-api-client/src/listings/hooks.ts:146-169 — useToggleFavorite's mutationFn does `if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Failed to toggle favorite')` and defines ONLY onSuccess (invalidateQueries); there is no onError. React Query captures the thrown rejection into mutation.isError state rather than surfacing it, so with no call-site handler the failure is fully silent — no toast, no console error, no rollback.

Impact: on the homepage and all featured ListingCards, a favorite toggle that fails (e.g. 401 when unauthenticated, or a network error) shows nothing to the user; the heart UI diverges from server state until the next listings refetch. UX/correctness gap on a conversion-critical public surface.

Inconsistency confirms this is a gap, not a convention: sibling mutation call sites DO handle errors — components/agency/RealtorManagement.tsx:570-580 (try/catch + setInviteError + i18n t('inviteError')), app/[locale]/saved-searches/page.tsx:140 and app/[locale]/inquiries/page.tsx:140 (render on mutation.isError).

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): component -> hook path fully read; route is public and reachable; classified medium severity because the action is non-destructive (favorite toggle) rather than data loss.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): surface toggleFavorite.isError (inline message/toast) or add an onError to the mutate call; optionally add optimistic rollback. Single-package reality-web edit; verifies with typecheck/test + biome.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/favorites/PriceAlerts.tsx:170,190 — markAllRead.mutate() and markRead.mutate(alert.id) are fired with no onError, and the component never reads markRead.isError/markAllRead.isError. Note the asymmetry: the QUERY path is fully handled (isLoading skeleton at :85, error state at :105, empty state at :123), but the two mutations have no failure surface at all.

Hook contract traced: frontend/packages/reality-api-client/src/favorites/hooks.ts:293-328 — both useMarkFavoriteAlertRead and useMarkAllFavoriteAlertsRead do `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(...)` and define only onSuccess (invalidateQueries FAVORITE_ALERTS_KEY); neither defines onError. The thrown rejection is swallowed into mutation.isError with no call-site reader, so a failed mark-read is silent.

Impact: a user clicking 'Mark read' / 'Mark all read' on a failed request sees the button re-enable with the alert still unread and no error shown — they cannot tell the action failed. Trust/clarity gap on the price-alert surface (Story 84.3).
Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): component -> hook path fully read; lower impact than the favorite toggle since the operation is non-destructive and retryable.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): render an inline error when markRead.isError || markAllRead.isError (mirror the existing isError branches in saved-searches/page.tsx:140 and inquiries/page.tsx:140). Single-package reality-web edit; verifies with typecheck/test + biome.
